newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger but underperform on data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger but underperform on data.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended stronger on Thursday, but underperformed their U.S. counterparts following the release of weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data, analysts said.

"The tone of the market is quite firm and was helped today by the durable goods order from the U.S.," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with I.D.E.A. "Canada has been lagging the U.S. We've been having some provincial supply."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.30 at C$103.25 to yield 7.709 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which rose 20/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 83 basis points from 81 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets rallied this morning after the U.S. Commerce department reported that August durable goods fell by a greater-than-expected 3.1 percent. The market was also buoyed by an unexpected rise in U.S. jobless claims data.
Canadian bonds underperformed in part because of new supply from the province of Saskatchewan and the prospect of more supply in the coming days, Kalirai said.

Saskatchewan this morning set a C$200 million, 6.125 percent bond due, October 10, 2001, said lead manager CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc. The issue was priced at C$99.025 to yield 6.356 percent with a spread of 10 basis points over the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due September, 2001.
The new supply from Saskatchewan follows a well-received C$350 million bond due October, 2001 issued on Wednesday by the province of Alberta.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.15 to C$98.91 to yield 7.151 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 9/32 to yield 6.65 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 50 basis points from 48 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.86 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.01 percent.
